text:
Sean Durzi missed nearly a month before the Rangers activated him off injured reserve on Nov. 22, and The Hockey News headline had him "Happy" to be back after a "Frustrating" injury. New York has gone straight back to leaning on him: 21:36 and 22:42 in his two games back, both losses. He has 5 points in 16 games in his first season on Broadway after playing for Utah.

What the Rangers want from him is the puck movement. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 6.2 primary shot assists per 60 last season, 89th percentile among defensemen, with 38% of his shots coming off the rush (a typical defenseman: 17%). The numbers this season are less kind. New York gets only 45% of the 5-on-5 chance quality with him on the ice, about 9 points worse than when he sits, and his 2 goals came on just 0.55 expected goals. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level in 2025-26. Our numbers project about 29 points; Forever Blueshirts says he's getting back in his groove.
headline: Sean Durzi is back, and the Rangers need his passing
